summary: Backend 10/10 pytest passing for notification prefs (GET/PATCH partial merge, DND on/off, mute-chat forever + unmute, non-member 404), memory access-rules CRUD (route ordering bug fix verified), PATCH /memory/{id} still works, approval→decision auto-creation works (memory_type=decision, meta.decision_status=approved, decision_history populated). Frontend /notifications page fully functional — all 4 sections render, DND dropdown writes through and shows 'Currently muted until…' status, mute-by-type toggles persist (Saved toast), email digest 'Weekly' persists, /you → Notifications row navigates correctly. No compile/runtime errors. ONE GAP found: /api/memory/search REST endpoint does NOT pass user_role to retrieve_memory, so role-based scope downgrade is only enforced via the AI ask path (routes/ai.py:73). Member can still query workspace memory via REST search.

minor.issue: Does not pass user_role to retrieve_memory(). Role-based scope downgrade (can_use_workspace_memory=false) is bypassed when member uses /api/memory/search?mode=workspace directly. Only AI ask flow enforces the rule. Add `user_role=current.get('role')` in routes/memory.py:search_memory call (line 45) to close this gap.

issues: DND init logic in NotificationsPrefs.jsx line 28 is a 'best-effort' that always maps existing dnd_until to '8h' label — if user originally chose 24h or 1week, the dropdown shows 8h on reload (cosmetic; functional truth lives in dnd_until ISO string shown in the status line). Consider storing the chosen duration in prefs or deriving from remaining time.

action_items: OPTIONAL/MINOR: Wire user_role into routes/memory.py:search_memory so /api/memory/search honors per-role access rules (currently only the AI ask path enforces them). One-line fix: pass user_role=current.get('role') into retrieve_memory().
critical_code_review_comments: Route ordering fix in routes/memory.py is correctly applied: /memory/access-rules GET/PATCH declared BEFORE /memory/{memory_id} so the parametric route no longer shadows it. Verified working (returned 200 instead of prior 404).

approvals.py:decide_approval wraps record_memory + extract_smart_cards in a broad try/except that swallows all exceptions silently — fine for production resilience but could hide failures during dev. Consider logging the exception.

Notification prefs are stored as a single embedded doc on users.notification_prefs. mute_chats grows unbounded if user mutes many chats forever. Add a periodic cleanup task to drop entries whose ISO until is in the past (currently kept indefinitely).
NotificationsPrefs.jsx uses optional chaining well; loading state is handled. Toast for mute-groups says generic 'Saved' — could echo which field changed for clarity.
/notifications/dnd uses query param (?duration=8h) instead of JSON body which mixes conventions with /notifications/prefs (PATCH json). Cosmetic — works fine.
